makeup: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation until earned

exophase.label: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official names, descriptions, grades)

psnprofiles.label: PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophies (PSN progress counts)

own.label: Our own advice, written from the official description — no location or step is claimed beyond what the description states

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order: story first, then stranger strands, then collectibles, then activities, and finish with the money and combat clean-up. The two gold trophies (the final mission and 100% completion) are the last gates before this one.
steps: Finish the story (Chapters 1-4 and the final mission).
Complete all stranger strands and side missions.
Sweep collectibles, activities and the money trophies, then check 100% completion.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This is the opening mission, Gone Fishing, so it unlocks naturally as you start the story — it cannot be missed. Just follow the opening objectives until the mission completes. It is the first trophy most players earn, and a good moment to tick it off in the tracker.
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Follow the on-screen objectives until the mission ends.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1's story missions in order; the trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission ends. Nothing in a chapter trophy is missable in itself — completing the chapter is the whole requirement. If you are hunting efficiently, do the chapter's side content later and keep the story moving.
steps: Play every story mission in Chapter 1 in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 by finishing its story missions in order. Like the other chapter trophies, this one only asks that the chapter be finished, so there is no special step or hidden condition — keep playing the story and it pops at the chapter's end.
steps: Play every story mission in Chapter 2 in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 by finishing its story missions in order. By this point the story is opening up Vice City itself, so use the chapter to learn the map — the exploration and vehicle trophies later reward knowing it well. The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission ends.
steps: Play every story mission in Chapter 3 in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale. Finish its story missions in order and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. Once this is done, only the final mission stands between you and the story gold — and the post-story clean-up can begin.
steps: Play every story mission in Chapter 4 in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission after Chapter 4. This is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the story — after it, the whole map stays open for clean-up. Before starting it, finish any stranger strands or partner moments you still want, just in case the post-story state changes who is available.
steps: Complete Chapters 1-4.
Finish any stranger strands you still want first.
Play and complete the final mission.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in the story. Mission trophies only ask that the named mission be finished — there is no extra objective to chase inside it. If a mission ever feels hard, the game lets you retry it, and the trophy still counts on completion.
steps: Reach Breakfast Run in the story.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games usually have a setup phase first — do the setups as they appear, then the heist itself. The trophy pops when the heist mission completes, whatever approach you take inside it.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in the story.
Do its setup steps as they appear, then complete the heist.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it appears. Like the other mission trophies, finishing the mission is the whole requirement — no side objective inside the mission is needed for it. Keep the story moving and it pops on completion.
steps: Reach Child's Play in the story.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners when it appears. The name suggests a big set-piece moment, but the trophy itself only needs the mission finished. Play it at whatever pace suits you — the trophy pops at the mission's end.
steps: Reach Headliners in the story.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Finishing the mission is all it asks — there is no extra airport objective hidden in it. Note the VCIA setting: the airport also matters for the missable trophy Catch Me If You Can, so pay attention to one-off moments while you are there.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in the story.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory when it appears. The trophy pops when the mission ends, with no extra condition. It is one of the later named missions, so by the time you reach it you are well into the story — keep pushing toward the finale from here.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the game's own checklist of story, side content, collectibles and activities, tracked in the pause menu's stats. This is the second gold trophy and the last gate before the platinum. Save it for last: work through this guide's roadmap stages and watch the in-game completion percentage climb, then mop up whatever category is still short.
steps: Finish the story and all stranger strands.
Complete the collectibles, activities and exploration trophies.
Check the in-game stats for the remaining percentage and finish that category.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near-misses, drifts and air time all count toward the total, and PSN tracks the count up to 250. This is a grind best done passively: play aggressively while doing everything else and the number climbs on its own. For the last stretch, find a long open road or a jump you can repeat, and use a fast, light vehicle.
steps: Play aggressively — jumps, drifts and near-misses all add up.
Check the PSN count (250) in the trophy list as you go.
Grind the remainder on a repeatable jump or long straight.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — PSN tracks the count to 9. The activity types are the game's side pastimes (races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, the shooting range, drone races and the like). You do not need to win or master any of them; one try of each is enough. Do this early so you know which activities you enjoy before grinding their trophies.
steps: Open the map and find one of each activity icon.
Try each activity once — winning is not required.
Tick it off when the PSN count reaches 9.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the PSN count is 42, so this is a big set. Visit the shooting range (shown on the map once unlocked) and work through the challenges weapon by weapon. Gold needs speed and accuracy together: learn each challenge's target pattern, retry the ones you miss, and upgrade or pick the weapon the challenge suits best. This is a silver for a reason — expect it to take a few focused sessions.
steps: Find the shooting range and open its challenge list.
Gold each challenge — learn the target pattern, then go for speed.
Retry missed challenges; the count is 42 in total.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks the count to 14. Drone races are a flying activity: learn each course's gates on a practice run, then race for the win. A win at a location counts once, so you need 14 wins at 14 different spots, not 14 wins anywhere. Clear them as you explore so the travelling does double duty.
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location on the map.
Learn the gates, then win the race there.
Repeat at all 14 locations.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses count, so repeating the same race does not help. Work through the race list across Leonida, using the fastest car you own for each surface, and take corners clean rather than fighting the pack. Races also feed the stunt and vehicle counts, so they are good grind material.
steps: Open the race list and pick an unwon course.
Win it with a car suited to the surface.
Repeat on 20 different courses.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head fishing contest, so it is about technique, not luck alone. Cast where the water is active, watch the line tension, and reel steadily instead of yanking. If you lose, challenge him again: the trophy only needs one win.
steps: Find Cal and start a fishing challenge.
Cast to active water and manage the line tension.
Win once — a loss just means challenging him again.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — any arcade cabinet counts, and finishing it is all it asks. Find an arcade (the map marks them once you are near one), pick a game, and play it through to its end or its high-score screen. This is one of the quickest trophies in the list.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet.
Play one game through to completion.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission — the last job in his mission strand. Contact strands unlock as the story progresses; play Andy's missions whenever his marker appears and the strand ends with this trophy. Do contact strands before the final story mission, in case the post-story state changes who is available.
steps: Play Andy's missions as his marker appears.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission — the last job in his strand. The name hints at a boat, so expect water in this one, but the trophy only needs the mission finished. Play Kenton's missions as they appear and finish the strand before the story's final mission.
steps: Play Kenton's missions as his marker appears.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission — the last job in his strand. The title points to riding alone, so a bike may feature, but the trophy only asks that the mission be completed. Clear Billy's strand before the final story mission, like the other contact strands.
steps: Play Billy's missions as his marker appears.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 8. Stranger markers appear on the map as you explore; each strand is a short chain of missions for one character. This is a silver because it takes real exploration: drive the whole state, check every stranger marker, and finish each strand you start. Aim to finish all 8 before the final story mission, in case any strand locks after the story ends.
steps: Explore Leonida and note every stranger marker.
Play each stranger's missions to the end of their strand.
Complete 8 strands in total.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission — the last job in his strand. Play Randy's missions whenever his marker appears and finish the strand before the story's final mission. Like the other contact trophies, completing the mission is the whole requirement.
steps: Play Randy's missions as his marker appears.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission — the last job in his strand. Play Tyrone's missions as they appear and finish the strand before the final story mission. The trophy pops when that last mission ends.
steps: Play Tyrone's missions as his marker appears.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 18. Meditation spots are scenic places, usually with a view; the game marks them once you are close. Work through them region by region with the map open, and tick each off here as you go so you can see which regions are still short.
steps: Explore Leonida region by region.
Meditate at each spot you find.
Repeat until the count reaches 18.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableNote: A unique animal may only appear once — save before the hunt.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a one-of-a-kind animal, not a common one, so you need to find Bret's specific target. This trophy is flagged missable because a unique animal may only appear once: save the game before you start the hunt, and if the animal escapes or the hunt fails, reload rather than letting the moment pass. The exact animal and spot are not pinned down by the official description, so follow Bret's directions in-game.
steps: Find Bret and take the hunting job.
Save the game before the hunt.
Track and take down the unique animal.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — cards are scattered across Leonida, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. This is a silver because it takes a full sweep: check shops, interiors and hidden corners as you explore, and trade or buy the cards you cannot find in the world. Track your sets here and finish the three easiest sets first.
steps: Collect cards as you explore Leonida.
Check which sets are closest to complete.
Finish 3 full sets.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — PSN tracks the count to 100, so this is one of the biggest sweeps in the list. WAiNK spots are spread across the whole state; do them as you travel for other trophies rather than as a separate 100-stop tour. Keep a region-by-region tally in your head (or in this tracker's notes) so the last dozen are easy to find.
steps: WAiNK It at every spot you pass while travelling.
Sweep region by region for the remainder.
Repeat until the count reaches 100.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's challenge list, tracked by PSN up to 50. Challenges cover driving, shooting, flying and more, and most complete naturally while you play. Open the challenge list, pick the easiest unfinished ones first, and leave the skill-based ones (like the shooting range golds) for a focused session.
steps: Open the in-game challenge list.
Clear the easiest unfinished challenges first.
Repeat until the count reaches 50.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you and escape the heat. You need your partner with you when the wanted level hits 4 stars, then you both have to break line of sight until the stars clear. Do it in the countryside, away from the city: build the wanted level with your partner in the car, then drive off-road and hide until the search ends. If your partner is not available, do it during a story moment when they are with you.
steps: Have your partner with you.
Raise your wanted level to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and hide until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you — do it while partner missions are available.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level. This trophy is flagged missable because it needs your partner beside you — do it while partner missions are available, before the story ends. Pick three shops close together, rob them one after another with your partner present, and keep moving: the hard part is keeping the wanted level alive across all three robberies, so do not let the stars clear between shops.
steps: Have your partner with you and pick 3 nearby shops.
Rob them one after another.
Keep your wanted level through all three — do not let it clear.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — PSN tracks the count to 100, so this is about variety, not ownership. Drive or sit in as many different vehicles as you can: cars, bikes, boats, trucks and anything unusual. Parking lots, dealerships and the road itself are all sources, and the count climbs fastest when you try a new vehicle every time you see one instead of sticking to your favourite.
steps: Drive a different vehicle every chance you get.
Check dealerships, lots and the road for new models.
Repeat until the count reaches 100.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-aim mode. Wait for a fight with a group of enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and drop five before it ends. The easiest moment is a mission or shootout where enemies cluster: do not waste it on one or two stragglers, and retry the encounter if you fall short.
steps: Find a fight with enemies grouped together.
Trigger Combat Focus.
Take down 5 enemies before it ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: A one-off airport moment — save before you try it, and do not leave VCIA the normal way first.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. This trophy is flagged missable because it describes a single, specific departure: the official description gives no second chance in words, so treat the moment as one-off. Save before you attempt it, and look for an unusual way out of the airport (a runway, a service road or a stolen plane) rather than leaving by the normal exit. If it does not pop, reload the save and try another exit.
steps: Go to VCIA and save the game first.
Find an unusual way to leave the airport grounds.
If it does not pop, reload and try another exit.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke about Rhinos — the tanks — and the trophy is about dealing with them. When a Rhino tank shows up (usually at high wanted levels or in a military area), take it on: the trophy pops for the encounter itself, not for a perfect run. Bring heavy weapons or explosives, keep moving so its cannon cannot track you, and do not try it on foot at close range.
steps: Reach a high wanted level or a military area to draw a Rhino.
Fight it with heavy weapons or explosives.
Keep moving and finish the encounter.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery. Go in quiet: move slowly, avoid the staff's line of sight, take the goods and leave before any alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting your way out. A quiet approach and a fast getaway car parked nearby make it far easier.
steps: Pick a jewelry store and park a fast car nearby.
Enter quietly and avoid being seen.
Take the goods and leave before any alarm.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — PSN tracks the count to 5, and each one needs a clean getaway. Plan each vault like a small heist: know the exit before you go in, have a fast car waiting, and lose the wanted level after each robbery before starting the next. The escape counts, so a vault robbed but not escaped does not add to the total.
steps: Find a bank vault and plan your exit first.
Rob it and escape with a fast car waiting.
Repeat at 5 different vaults.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — stop one, force it open, take the cash and get away before the police close in. A roadblock or a heavy vehicle to ram it works well; the escape is part of the trophy, so do not stop to fight once you have the money.
steps: Find an armored truck on its route.
Stop it, force it open and take the cash.
Escape and lose the wanted level.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 52 areas. The map fills in as you travel, so this trophy rewards driving everywhere: the city, the coast, the swamps and the small towns. Work through it region by region and use the in-game map to spot the blank patches you have not visited yet. It pairs naturally with the collectible sweeps.
steps: Drive through every region of Leonida.
Check the map for blank areas you have not visited.
Visit the last areas until the count reaches 52.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN tracks the count to 9. Each gang runs its own operations around Leonida; hitting one marks that gang off. Learn which operation belongs to which gang from the in-game markers, and work through them gang by gang so you can see which ones are left. Expect a fight at each one.
steps: Find an illegal operation and note which gang runs it.
Rob it and escape.
Repeat until all 9 gangs are covered.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — a quiet moment, not a challenge. Go to Ocean Beach, find a bar or vendor with a view of the water, and order a cocktail. It is one of the easiest trophies in the list and a good breather between the harder grinds.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Find a spot with a view of the water.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableNote: A one-off showroom smash — save before you try it.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. This trophy is flagged missable because it describes a single, specific smash-out: once you have left that showroom normally, the moment may be gone. Save before you try it, drive a car straight through the showroom glass, and if it does not pop, reload the save and try another showroom or another exit.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom and save first.
Drive through the showroom in a car.
If it does not pop, reload and try another exit.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — play a game of bowling there. You do not need a strike or a high score; playing through the game is what counts. It is a quick trophy and it also counts as one of the 9 activity types for Master of None.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play a game of bowling through to the end.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — the description is deliberately vague, and the official list gives no count for it. Read it as a partner moment: do something with your partner that draws a crowd or goes public, and the trophy pops when the partnership lands. The exact trigger is not pinned down by the description, so follow the partner activities in-game and watch for a big public moment together.
steps: Play partner activities when they appear.
Look for a public or crowd moment with your partner.
Complete it together.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: Story choices are one-way — PSN tracks 500 choices, so keep choosing; replaying a chapter may be the only way back.
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — PSN tracks a count up to 500, so this trophy is about making choices across the whole game, not one single decision. It is flagged missable because story choices are one-way: once you pick, that branch is gone unless you replay the chapter. Keep choosing whenever the game offers a choice — dialogue options, mission approaches, anything — and the count climbs. If you are near the end and still short, replay earlier chapters and choose differently.
steps: Choose whenever the game offers a choice.
Keep choosing across story and side content.
If still short near the end, replay a chapter and choose differently.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — the description points to succeeding on a retry. Fail something, then succeed at it on the next try, and the trophy pops. It will likely come naturally: a failed race, a missed shot or a blown challenge, then a clean second attempt. Do not force it — just keep playing, and retry anything you fail instead of moving on.
steps: Fail an attempt at something retryable.
Try it again right away.
Succeed on the second try.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableNote: A one-off strange encounter — save often while exploring odd spots.
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — the description points to a strange, one-off encounter somewhere in Leonida. It is flagged missable because a random or single-occurrence event may not repeat: save often while exploring unusual spots, and if something odd happens, stay with it until the trophy pops. The exact event is not pinned down by the official description, so explore the weird corners of the map — the swamps, the coast, the places that feel out of place.
steps: Explore Leonida's unusual spots.
Save often while exploring.
Stay with any strange event until it resolves.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing a melee weapon from the car, and the trophy pops when they go down. Do it somewhere quiet so the wanted level stays low, and retry if the swing misses.
steps: Get a melee weapon and a slow car.
Drive past a pedestrian and swing from the vehicle.
Retry if the swing misses.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and heists; your contacts clean them for a cut. Keep laundering after every big score instead of letting marked bills pile up, and the total climbs steadily. This pairs with the robbery trophies — every vault and truck you rob feeds it.
steps: Rob vaults, trucks and heists to collect marked bills.
Launder them through your contacts after each score.
Repeat until $250,000 is laundered.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — every shop in Leonida counts toward the total. Buy weapons, clothes, cars and upgrades as you play and the total climbs on its own; by the late game, big purchases like vehicles and properties push it over the line. Do not save-spend: the game tracks total spent, so normal shopping counts.
steps: Shop normally — weapons, clothes, cars, upgrades.
Make big purchases late in the game.
Repeat until $100,000 is spent.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN tracks the count to 8. Garages are bought from the in-game property listings once you have the money; each one also gives you somewhere to store the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good. Buy them as your funds allow, and save the most expensive ones for after the big heist payouts.
steps: Check the property listings for garages.
Buy each garage as funds allow.
Repeat until all 8 are owned.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game delivery app. Open the app, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until 10 are listed. It pairs with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you discover is a candidate to register, so do both trophies together.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app.
Register a vehicle.
Repeat until 10 vehicles are registered.

roadmap.title: Story first — Chapters 1-4 and the finale
roadmap.goal: Finish the story and take every mission trophy with it.
roadmap.note: Play the story missions in order. Mission trophies only need the named mission completed. Before the final mission, finish the stranger strands and partner moments in stage 2 — the post-story state may change who is available.

roadmap.title: Strangers and side strands
roadmap.goal: Clear all 8 stranger strands, the 5 contact finales and the choice count.
roadmap.note: Explore Leonida for stranger markers and play each strand to its end. Keep choosing whenever the game offers a choice — the choice count (500) climbs across the whole game.

roadmap.title: Collectibles sweep
roadmap.goal: Meditation spots, card sets, WAiNK locations, vehicles, areas, garages and Scooter Bros registrations.
roadmap.note: Sweep region by region with the map open. These counts are the longest grind after the story, so pair them with travel for other trophies.

roadmap.title: Activities and skill
roadmap.goal: Stunts, races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade, bowling and challenges.
roadmap.note: Try every activity once first (Master of None), then grind the counts: 250 stunts, 20 races, 14 drone race wins, 42 shooting range golds, 50 challenges.

roadmap.title: Money, combat and the platinum
roadmap.goal: Robberies, wanted-level moments, laundering, spending — then 100% completion.
roadmap.note: Do the missable moments first in this stage (Catch Me If You Can, Capital Offense, Retail Therapy). Finish with A Long Road (100%) and the platinum pops.
